name: Mktg.ai
summary: Always-on AI marketing analyst: unified creative visibility, live performance signals and plain-language questions over your own spend data. No public pricing, demo-first.
best_for: marketing teams with real media spend across channels who want an always-on AI analyst: every ad and post tied to its own spend and results, daily alerts and plain-language questions over their own data. It reads your accounts only and sits on top of your existing platforms, and the vendor offers a pilot on one brand and one or two paid channels for one reporting cycle
skip_if: your ad spend is modest (the value scales with budget waste, and yours is small), or you want transparent self-serve pricing before a sales call
honest_knock: The price is still not readable. The pricing page now exists, but it loads its content in the browser and the served page carries no figure, which is an odd look for a tool that sells spend transparency. The homepage business case has changed too: the $5M illustration we quoted earlier is gone, replaced by three client results ($26.7K of spend behind very low scoring TikTok ads at a CPG brand, $0.48 against $1.34 per click at a financial services brand, 30 of 33 franchises at a real estate brand) and a savings calculator the site itself calls an estimate. Those are the vendor's own numbers; ask for references at your spend level.

pricing.notes: No readable public price (re-verified 18 November 2026). mktg.ai/pricing no longer returns 404: it now serves a page titled 'mktg.ai pricing | What it costs and what you get', and the site also has an 'Enterprise Pricing' page, but both load their content in the browser and the served HTML carries no figure, so we publish no amount. The FAQ names Growth and Enterprise above the entry level: both include a dedicated customer success manager, SLA-backed response times and quarterly business reviews, and email support is on every plan. EU data residency is Enterprise-only, with US data centres the default. The site offers a pilot (one brand, one or two paid channels, one reporting cycle) and does not say whether it is paid. The llms.txt describes the product and carries no price.

open_questions.question: Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
